requirement:
For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.

For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
rationale:
The tests adequately cover `requirements.authoring.cache_checkpoints`. I did not read the `bedrock_run` and `without_cache_points` helpers; I took them to do what their names and use in the test suggest.

**Explicit-checkpoint backends.** Bedrock is the only backend that gets checkpoints. `RigProvider::connect` sets `caches` from `bedrock_caches` for Bedrock and to false for Ollama and OpenAI.

- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[claude_requests_carry_cache_checkpoints_and_record_cache_usage]` runs a full two-request Claude-on-Bedrock conversation against a fixture server. For every request body it asserts the following.
  - The `system` array has exactly two entries: the system text, which starts with "# Task", then the `cachePoint` block.
  - The last message's content ends with the `cachePoint` block.
  - The body contains exactly two `cachePoint` occurrences, so there is one after the system prompt, one at the end of the last message, and no others.
- That test also covers the second request, which has three messages and follows a reasoning turn. It still ends in a checkpoint, so "every provider request" and the growing conversation are both exercised.
- Checkpoints must not change content. The same test runs an uncached fixture model (`fixture-uncached-model`) and asserts that the cached bodies, once `without_cache_points` strips the checkpoints, equal the uncached bodies request by request.
- The "when the backend and model support prompt caching" condition is covered in two places.
  - The test above asserts the uncached model's request has no `cachePoint`.
  - `providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cache_checkpoints_are_requested_for_caching_models]` asserts `bedrock_caches` is true for Claude (plain and inference-profile ARN) and Nova, and false for Llama and an unknown model.
- That unit test also checks that `place_cache_checkpoints` only sets `options.cache`, by comparing the serialized request with an expected one. It also checks that the option is set after a reasoning turn.

**OpenAI.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[openai_responses_replays_tool_calls_and_records_usage]` runs two requests.

- A recursive `assert_no_checkpoints` check on every request body rejects `cachePoint` and `cache_control` keys and `cache_point` or `cache_checkpoint` block types. This covers "MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks".
- `instructions` are non-empty and identical across the two requests, and `tools` are identical. This covers keeping the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged.
- The second request's `input` starts with the first request's `input`, unchanged and in order. After that prefix come the `function_call` and `function_call_output` items for call `read`. This covers replaying prior content in its original order.

**Gaps.** I found none. Nova is tested only at the `bedrock_caches` family-detection level, not end to end. It goes through the same code path as Claude, so that is not a distinct obligation. The citation of `prompt_parts` is context only, and the system-prompt structure it requires is also exercised here by the system-array assertions.

text: :::{req} cache_checkpoints
For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.
For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
:::{req} prompt_parts
Each assessment conversation MUST send its prompt as a system prompt followed by
one user message, the subject message, filled from the first and second text
blocks of the prompt requirement for the assessment's kind. The kinds are
test-adequacy requirement, structural requirement, example, citation review, site
review, and a verifier of each of those. A system prompt MUST be the same for
every assessment of its kind, so every placeholder whose value depends on the
subject MUST be in the subject message.
